cases.name: front-page
cases.note: The root alone.

cases.name: unreadable-cert-file
cases.stderr: warning: SSL_CERT_FILE is unreadable; trusting no certificates
cases.note: An unreadable explicit CA file warns once at startup; HTTP crawling continues.

cases.name: summary-last
cases.note: Every page line is on stdout before the summary is on stderr (DESIGN §2): 2>&1 shows the summary last.

cases.name: flags
cases.note: The small site the flag cases crawl.

cases.name: env-concurrency
cases.note: An environment concurrency value applies when no -c flag is given.

cases.name: fast-flag
cases.stderr: settings: fast, cpus 2, threads 2, concurrency 48 \(max 48\), delay 0s
cases.note: Fast mode uses this machine's capacity and starts without delay.

cases.name: verbose-settings
cases.stderr: settings: polite, cpus 2, threads 2, concurrency 1 \(max 48\), delay 1s, timeout 10s, pages 1000
cases.note: The verbose settings line uses the same words in every engine.

cases.name: affinity-cpus
cases.note: Without CRAWL_CPUS, taskset to two CPUs sets the machine's CPU count.

cases.name: affinity-quota
cases.note: Inside a two-CPU quota and four-CPU affinity, the quota sets the CPU count.

cases.name: relative-references
cases.note: A name, a dot, a parent, a root path, a query, a fragment, a scheme-relative link and a <base> that is ignored.

cases.name: kept-as-written
cases.note: What the URL form leaves alone: a trailing slash, an escape, a query's order.

cases.name: duplicate-links
cases.note: A page lists each link once, in the order it first appeared.

cases.name: duplicate-headers
cases.note: A repeated Content-Type, Location or Retry-After counts its first value (DESIGN §5).

cases.name: not-links
cases.note: What is no link: another scheme, a comment, a raw-text element, and every tag but <a>.

cases.name: scanned-elements
cases.note: What is scanned, unlike a browser's DOM: <noscript>, <iframe>, <template>, <xmp>, <svg>, CDATA, and a script's end tag inside its own string.

cases.name: comments
cases.note: A comment runs from <!-- to the next -->: <!--> does not end one, and --!> does not either (DESIGN §4).

cases.name: tag-syntax
cases.note: How a start tag is read: case, whitespace, quotes, a bare href, an empty one, a second href, and a stray quote that runs to its match.

cases.name: broken-markup
cases.note: A tag, a comment, a script or a quote never closed ends the page's links, quietly.

cases.name: character-references
cases.note: References as the HTML tokenizer reads an attribute value: named, numeric, without a semicolon, a legacy name before = or a letter, and a reference to nothing as U+FFFD.

cases.name: whitespace-in-hrefs
cases.note: Whitespace in an href or a Location: stripped at the ends, and a tab or newline inside removed, as the URL Standard does; a space inside percent-encoded.

cases.name: encoding
cases.note: The URL form's bytes, each component by its own percent-encode set (the URL Standard): UTF-8 and what a path or query may not hold encoded, a ' in a query too; escapes kept as written, a % that starts none kept; NUL and controls.

cases.name: url-form
cases.note: The URL Standard's parsing: scheme and host case, ports, http: without // as a relative reference, a backslash as a slash, dot segments and escaped dots, a host that is not ASCII (punycode) or holds an escape (decoded), an authority with no host.

cases.name: on-host
cases.note: The host is matched after the form: LOCALHOST is this host, another port or scheme is fetched, a trailing dot, an IP or a subdomain is another host. -t 2: the https link is answered by nothing, and waits.

cases.name: external-hosts
cases.note: A link off the host is listed and not crawled; a subdomain is off the host.

cases.name: userinfo
cases.note: A link with userinfo is no link: two engines' clients would send it as an Authorization header, and http://host:port@evil.example/ is the phishing form.

cases.name: redirects
cases.note: A 3xx lists its Location alone, resolved as an href: relative, with a fragment, to itself, a 308; a body, no Location, an empty or javascript: one list nothing.

cases.name: statuses
cases.note: Only a 2xx text/html body is read: a 201, 205, 206 or 299 is; a 404 with HTML, a PDF or plain text is not.

cases.name: bodiless-statuses
cases.note: A 204 or 304 has no body whatever its headers say (RFC 9112 6.3): the page is its status, with no error and no links, and the crawl goes on.

cases.name: content-types
cases.note: text/html by media type alone: case and parameters ignored, XHTML and a missing Content-Type not HTML, a Content-Type sent twice its first.

cases.name: framing
cases.note: Where a body ends (RFC 9112 §6.3): at the connection's end without a length, HTTP/1.0, chunks over a Content-Length, extensions and trailers, a 100 first, bytes past the length left.

cases.name: chunked-gzip-reuse
cases.note: A decoded gzip chunk leaves its zero chunk and trailers consumed before the next GET reuses the connection.

cases.name: body-limits
cases.note: 5 MiB exactly is read; one byte more, a chunked 6 MiB, or a Content-Length over it is 'body over 5 MiB'; fewer bytes than the length is 'body cut short'.

cases.name: latin1-page
cases.note: A body is bytes read as UTF-8: each byte that is not UTF-8 is U+FFFD in the link.

cases.name: utf16-page
cases.note: A UTF-16 body has no <a in its bytes: no links, no error.

cases.name: gzip-unasked
cases.note: Without Accept-Encoding a Content-Encoding is not decoded: a compressed body has no links.

cases.name: non-html-not-read
cases.note: A body that isn't HTML is never read: a PDF trickling one byte every 5 s costs nothing (read, it would take 110 s).

cases.name: links-limit-distinct
cases.note: The first 1,000 distinct links of a page, in order.

cases.name: links-limit-duplicates
cases.note: 1,006 hrefs of 503 distinct links: 503.

cases.name: links-limit-normalized
cases.note: Distinct after the URL form: /x, /x#a, x, ./x, /links-limit/../links-limit/x are one link; /x? and /%78 are others.

cases.name: links-byte-cap
cases.note: The first 254 resolved links use 261,510 bytes; the next would pass the 256 KiB link cap.

cases.name: stream-straddle
cases.note: An anchor spanning buffers is found; anchors in a long comment and script are skipped.

cases.name: long-tag
cases.note: A tag over 64 KiB gives no link; the following anchor still does.

cases.name: directory-index
cases.note: /dir/ and /dir/index.html are two pages: the form does not know a server's index file.

cases.name: retry-policy
cases.note: Up to five attempts for 408, 429, 502, 503, 504 and a dropped connection, none for a 500 or a 404, none when Retry-After passes the deadline (DESIGN §5): 120 s, past the largest -t, never fits. The jittered waits are at most 3.75 s a URL, so -t 60 only catches a hang: at the default -t 10 a wait that fit with a sliver left could have its attempt cut by the deadline on a loaded runner, a timeout in place of the label.

cases.name: retry-fast
cases.note: Under -f a retry delays only its own fetch; the other workers keep going (DESIGN §2, §5). The jittered waits are at most 3.75 s a URL, so -t 60 only catches a hang: at the default -t 10 a wait that fit with a sliver left could have its attempt cut by the deadline on a loaded runner, a timeout in place of the label.

cases.name: dropped-connections
cases.note: A connection dropped before a status line is retried, then an error; the crawl goes on. The jittered waits are at most 3.75 s a URL, so -t 60 only catches a hang: at the default -t 10 a wait that fit with a sliver left could have its attempt cut by the deadline on a loaded runner, a timeout in place of the label.

cases.name: dead-host
cases.note: Five refused connections in a row end the crawl with exit 1 and 'error: host unreachable'. Each page's refused connects are retried, with jittered waits of at most 3.75 s, so -t 60 only catches a hang: at the default -t 10 a wait that fit with a sliver left could have its attempt cut by the deadline on a loaded runner, a timeout in place of the label.

cases.name: stale-keepalive
cases.note: The server closes a kept-alive connection behind a whole answer: the next request on it is retried on a new one, not reported.

cases.name: timeout-mid-body
cases.note: A body that trickles past -t is 'timeout' with no status, though its headers came.

cases.name: timeout-stalled-body
cases.note: The headers arrive and the body stalls: -t still ends the fetch, and a timed-out page prints no status.

cases.name: max-pages
cases.note: -l bounds the pages fetched; the last page still lists its links.

cases.name: max-pages-one
cases.note: -l 1: the start page and its links, nothing crawled.

cases.name: start-unreachable
cases.note: Five refused connects are 'connect failed'. Port 1: no unprivileged process can listen there, where 59999, in Linux's ephemeral range, can be another test's port (a JVM's crawl timed out against one). The four waits are at most 3.75 s, so -t only catches a hang (-t 1 and -t 5 cut a slow JVM's last attempt).

cases.name: start-404
cases.note: A start page at or over 400 fails the crawl: exit 1, its links not read.

cases.name: start-redirect-external
cases.note: A 3xx start page is not a failure: its Location is listed, off the host, and the crawl ends clean.

cases.name: start-uppercase
cases.note: The start URL is printed in the form: scheme and host lowercased.

cases.name: start-no-slash
cases.note: A start URL with no path is the root.

cases.name: flag-leading-zero
cases.note: A flag's value is decimal digits: 08 is 8, and leading zeros are any number.

cases.name: flag-thousands-suffix
cases.note: An uppercase K suffix is accepted, and a later occurrence of the flag overrides it.

cases.name: sigint-drains
cases.note: The first signal stops dispatching; the fetch in flight completes and prints.

cases.name: sigint-twice-exits
cases.note: A second signal exits at once, the fetch in flight abandoned (DESIGN §2).

cases.name: sighup-ends
cases.note: SIGHUP is not handled: its default ends the crawl at once (DESIGN §2).

cases.name: sigpipe-ignored
cases.note: A SIGPIPE sent to the crawler is ignored: the crawl goes on and ends clean (DESIGN §2).

cases.name: closed-pipe
cases.note: stdout closed by its reader (crawl | head) ends the crawl with exit 0.

cases.name: tls-graph
cases.note: 200 pages over TLS 1.3 and HTTP/1.1 from a server that speaks HTTP/2 too: the crawler offers http/1.1 alone by ALPN (DESIGN §5).

cases.name: tls12
cases.note: tls-graph's 200 pages from a server of TLS 1.2 alone and an ECDSA certificate.

cases.name: tls12-rsa
cases.note: tls-graph's 200 pages from a server of TLS 1.2 alone and an RSA certificate.

cases.name: tls13-rsa
cases.note: tls-graph's 200 pages from a server of TLS 1.3 alone and an RSA certificate.

cases.name: wire
cases.note: At one request in flight, no other retry can extend the shared gate: verify the target, headers, bounded backoff after two 503s, and Retry-After: 1 (DESIGN §1, §5). The jittered waits are at most 3.75 s a URL, so -t 60 only catches a hang: at the default -t 10 a wait that fit with a sliver left could have its attempt cut by the deadline on a loaded runner, a timeout in place of the label.

cases.name: wire-tls
cases.note: The same over TLS.

cases.name: deadline-after-throttle
cases.note: The -t deadline starts after the throttle wait (DESIGN §5): 8 queued workers at 0.5 s apart outlast a 1 s timeout, and none times out.

cases.name: help lists the contract's flags
help_contains: fast: as many requests as this machine takes, no delay
requests in flight at most      (default 1, 1 to 256)

cases.name: -h after a bad value (-c 0 -h)
cases.note: -h wins over a value out of its range: the ranges are checked once every flag is read.

cases.name: hold-on-429
cases.note: A 429 with Retry-After: 1 holds every new request start until that second ends. The mock orders its answers by events, not delays (mock/timing.ts); -t and the wall only catch a hang.

cases.name: hold-on-502
cases.note: A retried 502 with Retry-After: 1 pauses new requests at the same gate. The mock orders its answers by events, not delays (mock/timing.ts); -t and the wall only catch a hang.

cases.name: delay-spaces-requests
cases.note: At -c 8, starts are 100 ms apart. The mock stamps the root as it answers it, before any leaf can start, and a leaf no earlier than it started: the four leaves' starts span 300 ms, so 200 ms between the stamps holds whatever the plugin's or the crawler's speed. The wall only catches a hang (5 s failed a loaded JVM's).

cases.name: mid-headers
cases.note: Headers cut off before their end: an error, or (the JDK, which cannot tell it from a body that ends with the connection) an empty page; never a hang.

cases.name: tcp-reset
cases.note: The reset keeps its failure label through retries. The four waits are at most 3.75 s, so -t only catches a hang: at -t 5 a retry that fit with a sliver left was cut by the deadline on a loaded runner, and printed timeout.

cases.name: content-length-neg
cases.note: A negative content-length is a malformed head, retried: the four waits are at most 3.75 s, so -t only catches a hang (at -t 5 a wait that fit with a sliver left could have its attempt cut, and print timeout).

cases.name: gzip-bomb
cases.note: A compressed body that would be gigabytes: decompressing it stops at MAX_BODY_BYTES with body over limit and exits 1.

cases.name: retry-after-neg
cases.note: A Retry-After that is no whole number of seconds is ignored: the jittered waits, at most 3.75 s, then the last 503. -t only catches a hang: at -t 3 a wait that fit with a sliver left had its attempt cut by the deadline, and printed timeout.

cases.name: retry-after-float
cases.note: A Retry-After that is no whole number of seconds is ignored: the jittered waits, at most 3.75 s, then the last 503. -t only catches a hang: at -t 3 a wait that fit with a sliver left had its attempt cut by the deadline, and printed timeout.

cases.name: retry-after-date
cases.note: A Retry-After that is no whole number of seconds is ignored: the jittered waits, at most 3.75 s, then the last 503. -t only catches a hang: at -t 3 a wait that fit with a sliver left had its attempt cut by the deadline, and printed timeout.

cases.name: dns-nonexistent
cases.note: A name that does not resolve is dns failed, retried: the four waits are at most 3.75 s, so -t only catches a hang (at -t 2, under the waits' 3.75 s, an attempt the deadline cut printed timeout in place of dns failed).

cases.name: mem-tree
cases.note: What 1500 pages of a 32-link tree cost in memory. The wall is for a crawl that has stopped, not a speed: 1500 pages is few enough that the JVM is still compiling, and the gate runs every language's tests at once.

cases.name: flag-twice
cases.note: A flag given twice keeps its last value (DESIGN §1).

cases.name: obs-fold
cases.note: An obsolete line fold: the client accepts or refuses it, never hangs.

cases.name: lf-only
cases.note: Bare LF between headers: the client's own.

cases.name: http09
cases.note: No status line at all: an error, never a page.

cases.name: status-2000
cases.note: A four-digit status is no status: an error, never 2000 and never 200.

cases.name: headers-endless
cases.note: Headers that never end: the client's own limit cuts them, within memory.

cases.name: mem-c128-2mib
cases.note: 128 bodies of 2 MiB in flight: what wide concurrency costs, under the cap

cases.name: mem-c256-5mib
cases.note: 256 bodies of exactly 5 MiB in flight: streaming keeps each fetch under 512 KiB.

cases.name: mem-m-max
cases.note: The largest -l allocates nothing for pages that never come.

cases.name: queue-overflow
cases.note: A thousand links a page fill the 128 MiB queue: links are dropped, the crawl goes on to -l.

cases.name: slowloris
cases.note: Every connection stalls: -t ends the fetches in flight together, not one after another (Java crawls at the -c its heap allows).

cases.name: overloaded-server
cases.note: A server that answers four requests at once sheds the rest with a 503 and Retry-After: every page still comes.

cases.name: tls-untrusted
cases.note: A certificate the trust store does not accept fails the start page: exit 1, no hang.

cases.name: tls-handshake-reset
cases.note: A handshake the server resets is tls failed, after its four retries. The four waits are at most 3.75 s, so -t only catches a hang: at -t 5 a retry that fit with a sliver left could be cut by the deadline on a loaded runner (a JVM's five handshakes and their backoff took over 2 s on a two-core one), and print timeout.

cases.name: graph-whole
cases.note: A whole site of 1,500 pages: every engine prints the same set, with the same links on each page.

cases.name: calendar-trap
cases.note: An endless calendar: the first 200 pages in breadth-first order are the same everywhere.

cases.name: crawlme-hostile

raw:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8
connection: close
transfer-encoding: chunked

zz
not a chunk size

cases.comment: Nothing of its own to expect: what a crawler prints for a dead socket is a spec decision, not something Scrapy, Heritrix or Nutch can vouch for. A page that is not damaged must match crawlme; a damaged one is not compared. A page survives when some route to it avoids every damaged page, which does not depend on traversal order, so every implementation reaches the same count. -c 128 and -t 2 hold it to seconds: every fault still ends its page as at -t 5 (a stall in a timeout, a 503 in a 503, a drop in its retries), and none of it depends on order.

cases.name: intl
cases.note: A generated site of what the recording never has: paths and queries in other scripts and with spaces, escapes kept, relative and absolute redirects, missing pages, links off the host and with fragments. Its expected file is Scrapy's (e2e/oracle/), so nothing under test wrote it.
